title: Cwm-Cedwyn in the 1392 Llandough bounds
text: Cwm-Cedwyn is named in Llandough boundary records of 1392 (family research note; document not yet held).

title: Herbert's 1,000-year grant to Vaughan
text: Sir George Herbert granted Vaughan a 1,000-year lease of Cydwin in 1547 (family research note; verification pending). A 1,000-year term from 1547 would still be running.

title: The farm framed as a manorial leasehold
text: NLW D219, 'Llandough manorial leases and agreements, 1552–1829', lists leases of 'Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)'. Leases place a manorial lord above the occupier.

title: The chief freehold farm of the parish
text: 'Great House was the chief freehold farm of the parish and was occupied by the Vaughan's, a minor gentry family, from the mid C16 until the latter part of the C18.'
source: HER GGAT02038s, as quoted by RCAHMW https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/rcahmw-correspondence/

title: Vaughan memorials in Llandough churchyard
text: Edward Vaughan 'of this parish, gent.' died 2 June 1722 aged 79; Edmond Vaughan, gent., died 1770 aged 79; 'Ricardus Vaughan, armiger' died at Cardiff in 1835 aged 56.

title: 'Farmed by her family since 1667'
text: In November 1958 the Western Mail reported Mrs M. D. Buckler's objection that land farmed by her family since 1667 had been 'wrongfully appropriated' (OCR; page image not yet seen).

title: Llandough manor sold to Bute
text: Llandough manor was sold to the Bute estate in 1793 for £19,000 (reported; NLW D95/32–6 not yet inspected). A manor sale carries the lordship and the lands its deed lists.

title: 'The freehold was acquired by the Bute Estate'
text: The HER states that in the early 19th century 'the freehold was acquired by the Bute Estate'. No deed is cited for the acquisition.
source: HER GGAT02038s, as quoted by RCAHMW https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/rcahmw-correspondence/

title: Manorial courts held in Great House
text: '…the manorial courts for Llandough and Leckwith were held in Great House.' The house was the manorial court-house of two parishes.
source: HER GGAT02038s, as quoted by RCAHMW https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/rcahmw-correspondence/

title: Tŷ Mawr recorded as Bute estate plan 19
text: Bute's 1824 survey lists 'Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm' as plan 19, tenant John Gedrick (reading), 139a 3r 8p including 20a 2r 35p of wood.

title: 'Late Thos. Williams' in the Tŷ Mawr row
text: The same 1824 table reads 'Late Thos. Williams now John Gedrick Tent.' for a 10a 3r 39p unit added into Tŷ Mawr: the earliest Williams name on the holding found so far.

title: Tithe: Bute named landowner
text: The c.1841 tithe apportionment names 'Bute the Marquess of' as landowner of 33 parcels of the holding.

title: John Williams occupies 36 parcels in two parishes
text: c.1841 John Williams occupied 36 parcels, 119a 2r 30p, in Llandough and Leckwith, including no. 209 'Courtyard &c'.

title: The glebe cottage
text: John Williams also occupied three glebe parcels from the rector, including no. 196 'Cottage & garden'. In 1872 he was rated for glebe land of the Rev. H.H. Rickards.

title: Succession in 1855
text: John Williams 'succeeded his father in the tenancy of the farm in 1855' and attended his 102nd Bute rent audit in 1904 (the paper states 'Llandough Farm'; match to Great House is an inference).

title: 'Williams John, Great house'
text: Six trade directories, 1868–1901, list 'Williams John, Great house', Llandough.

title: Pwllypant (Caerphilly) Williams estate passes to Bute
text: The 3rd Marquess 'received the Pwllypant estate from W. E. Williams as a bequest in 1870' and 'divided the personal estate amongst Williams's relations'. No link to the Llandough Williams is shown.

title: Rate books: farm under Lord Bute
text: 1870s poor-rate books: 'John Williams | Lord Bute | Farm', about 76 acres; Lord Bute rated for 32 acres of woods in hand (provisional reading).

title: The 1877 Bute–Thomas sale
text: The farmhouse, buildings and about 10 acres were sold by Bute to Daniel Thomas; 'when the quarrying ceased the freehold should belong to my grandfather'.

title: No 1877 deed located
text: No copy of the 1877 Bute–Thomas agreement or plan has been located in any archive or registry searched; the family copy was kept in the farmhouse blanket box.
source: EV-0006 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0006-bute-thomas-agreement-1877/; Mary (Nancy) Williams, witness statement c.1974 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/

title: Leckwith-with-Llandough left to Lord Colum
text: The 3rd Marquess's will left his estates in Leckwith with Llandough to Lord Colum Crichton-Stuart. How the land returned to the 1938 vendor is not shown.

title: Father takes over the farm
text: 'In the year 1908 my grandfather died and my father took over the farm.'

title: 'Tenancy of the whole of the farm'
text: Court of Appeal: 'in February 1916 the Marquis granted a yearly agricultural tenancy of the whole of the farm to a Mr John Williams'. The 1916 document and plan are not held.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: WW1 ploughing quotas for Llandough and Leckwith
text: The Glamorgan War Agricultural Committee set 1916 arable figures and ploughing quotas for Llandough (parish 123) and Leckwith (124), with cultivation notices in 1917.

title: WW1 cultivation notices and appeals
text: Cardiff area District Survey 1916–18: list of cultivation notices (Mar–Apr 1917), appeals (Sep–Dec 1917), farms where ploughing was unfinished on 16 Mar 1918. Whether Tŷ Mawr appears is not yet seen.

title: WAEC objections file naming Leckwith
text: County Clerk's War Agricultural Executive Committee objections file, 1918–21, includes Leckwith, 'specifying names of appellants, names of farm, requirements'.

title: Bute–Corbett drain agreement
text: A 15 May 1924 drain agreement and plan between the Marquis of Bute and James Pelham Stuart Corbett sits on the Great House first-registration file (WA231076 item 2).

title: Mountjoy Ltd and the Leckwith farm sales
text: In 1926 the remaining Bute property went into Mountjoy Ltd; Leckwith was a Cardiff Castle manor 'to 1926 when the farms were sold off'.
source: Glamorgan Archives DA description; Michaelston-le-Pit & Leckwith CC village history page

title: 1928: quarrying ends, last rent paid
text: 1928 the quarry machinery left and the last rent was paid to Alfred Thomas; on the 1877 terms the freehold then passed to the Williams family. The receipt is not held.
source: Mary (Nancy) Williams, witness statement c.1974 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/; EV-0016 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0016-1928-last-rent-receipt-quarrying/

title: 1877 and 1928 absent from the 1987 judgment
text: The Court of Appeal judgment contains no mention of 1877, 1928, Daniel or Alfred Thomas, or the quarry (word search of the full text). Its chain begins in 1916.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: 1938 reversion to Western Ground Rents
text: 'In 1938 the reversion on that tenancy was conveyed to … Western Ground Rents Ltd.' WGR's root was later recited as 'a Conveyance on sale dated 25th December 1938'. Deed and plan not held.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; EV-0216 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0216-1965-contract-condition-f-conveyance-25-december-1938/

title: 1938 sale described as urban leaseholds
text: Glamorgan Archives describes the 1938 sale as WGR buying 'the urban leaseholds of the Bute Glamorgan Estate'; another catalogue records that Mountjoy sold 'its leasehold interests'.

title: 1939 grazing let: plan shows Parcel B only
text: WGR's May 1939 monthly let to John Williams, 8s a month 'as meadow or pasture land': the held plan page shows Parcel B only, highlighted.

title: WW2 War Agricultural Executive Committee powers
text: WAECs could 'take possession of land and … requisition, inspect and enter property' (TNA guide). Glamorgan WAEC minutes 1939–41 and executive papers 1941–45 survive.
source: TNA research guide https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/help-with-your-research/research-guides/land-requisitioned-war/ ; Glamorgan Archives DSA/43/3 https://canfod.glamarchives.gov.uk/en/records/DSA/43/3

title: Leckwith Woods gift and military requisition
text: WGR gave about 109 acres of Leckwith Woods to Cardiff council (1940–42); 'part of the site was requisitioned by the military authorities'. Measured outline: 0 ha in Llandough.

title: National Farm Survey of the parishes
text: 1941–43 farm survey forms for Leckwith (MAF 32/1213/33) and Penarth (MAF 32/1220/39) and the annotated sheet XLVII map (MAF 73/58/47) exist; not yet seen.

title: The War Agricultural Committee's pressure
text: 'During the war my father had difficulty in farming the land to the satisfaction of the War Agricultural Executive Committee, owing to his age and in 1944 it was arra[nged]…' that Frederick took on the farming.

title: Water cut off for nearly 10 years
text: Western Mail, 20 Nov 1958: 'the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents'; also the 'loss of a complete herd of Friesian cattle' (snippets).

title: 1949 surrender and re-grant
text: CA: John Williams 'fell into arrears with his rent in the mid-1930s and in the late 1940s'; his tenancy was surrendered and a new yearly tenancy from 2 Feb 1949 granted to Frederick Buckler.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: 1949: the farmhouse tenancy refused
text: The wiki records that the 1949 tenancy concerned Parcel B, and that Mary refused a tenancy of the farmhouse at the same time and asserted ownership (refusal: source pending).

title: Title papers removed, 1950–52
text: Title papers kept in the farmhouse blanket box with the 1877 agreement disappeared in 1950–52 (statement of Mary (Nancy) Williams; GHF-E123).
source: Mary (Nancy) Williams, witness statement c.1974 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/; GHF-E123 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/ghf-e123-family-title-papers-removed-c-1950-52/

title: Mountjoy disposes of the Glamorgan manors
text: 1950–57: disposal of Glamorgan manors by Mountjoy Ltd, with 'schedules of manorial property including details of rents, schedule of common land'.

title: WGR: 'not proceeding with the letting'
text: CA records a letter from WGR's agents of 10 October 1952 saying they did not propose to proceed with the letting.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: 1954 attempt to treat Frederick as tenant
text: A further attempt in 1954 to place Frederick in the position of a tenant did not succeed (GHF-E182; original document not yet located).

title: Adverse possession only from 1955
text: The appeal's primary case ran adverse possession of the farmhouse and garden 'from, at latest, February 2 1955' — the end of a tenancy whose 1939 plan shows Parcel B only.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; EV-0023 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0023-1939-wgr-john-williams-tenancy-plan/

title: 1955 execution of the whole-farm order
text: WGR obtained an Order 14 possession order 'in respect of the whole of the farm'; on 4 July 1955 possession was taken of 'all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden'.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: The farmhouse held in 1955
text: The order was not enforced against the farmhouse and garden: Mary had recently come out of hospital after a leg amputation. The family stayed in the house.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: Cardiff holds 176 acres of Leckwith Woods
text: By 1955 Cardiff held a 176-acre Leckwith Woods 'bought … for a nominal sum'.

title: 'A slice of land' from Lord Bute
text: Leckwith Common inquiry: 'About 130 years ago Lord Bute allowed her family “a slice of land” which was now Leckwith Common.'

title: Leckwith Common orders
text: Leckwith Common: Commons Act 1899 enclosure and extinguishment of rights (1949–61), encroachments under the Law of Property Act 1925 (1935–59), the 1957 compulsory purchase order.

title: Cogan Pill acquisition names WGR owner
text: A September 1958 Glamorgan County Council acquisition notice near Cogan Pill lists Western Ground Rents as owner.

title: 'A Welsh case of Crichel Down'
text: 'This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down … The Glamorgan County Council, Penarth Urban and Cardiff Rural Councils and Western Ground Rents have walked …' (snippet breaks off).

title: 'Conceived the notion' of title
text: CA: she 'had conceived the notion that she had a title to the ownership of Great House Farm through her own grandfather … No such documents were, however, ever produced.'
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: Tenancy and rehousing refused
text: She 'was offered a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden by Western Ground Rents but refused to accept it. She was also later offered, and refused, alternative accommodation.'
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: WGR / Brick & Tile / Cardiff deed
text: A 29 March 1961 deed with plan between WGR, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City may concern the later woodland title area. Not yet inspected.

title: 1962 possession order
text: Cardiff County Court possession order of 11 December 1962 (farmhouse and garden). Held enforceable until December 1974.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; EV-0041 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0041-cardiff-county-court-possession-order-1962/

title: Suspended committal order
text: CA: 'there seems to have been a suspended committal order against Mr Frederick Buckler in June 1963'.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: BP admits adverse possession 1965–74
text: 'It is admitted for BP Properties Ltd that Mrs Buckler was in adverse possession from her husband's death in 1965-67 until October 31 1974.'
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: Weekly tenancy offered again
text: In March 1965 WGR's agents offered Mary (Nancy) Williams a tenancy; it was not signed and no rent was paid.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; EV-0039 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0039-wgr-tenancy-offers-1959-1965/

title: WGR sells to BP Pension Trust
text: December 1969: Great House Farm, 'including the farmhouse and garden', sold by WGR to BP Pension Trust. The deed is on neither HM Land Registry first-registration file.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; EV-0043 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0043-wgr-bp-pension-trust-conveyance/

title: Village green registration VG41
text: The south-east ground was registered as village green VG41 on 16 June 1970. Registration did not by itself vest the green in anyone.

title: 1974: ownership pleaded
text: In BP Pension Trust's 1974 action, Mary (Nancy) Williams pleaded ownership and that BP's claim was barred. That action 'has never been finally heard'.
source: EV-0049 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0049-mary-williams-plea-ownership-pleadings/; BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: Leave to enforce on two days' notice
text: 17–19 Sep 1974: BP Pension Trust, 'as successors in title to Western Ground Rents', obtained leave to execute the 1962 order while its own action was part-heard.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: The unilateral licence letters
text: Two letters of 31 Oct 1974 offered to let Mrs Buckler stay for life. 'Mrs Buckler therefore never expressly accepted or rejected the terms of the two letters.'
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; EV-0050 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0050-1974-bp-licence-letters/

title: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement
text: Her typed statement of c.1974 sets out the 1877 agreement, the end of rent in 1928, the War Agricultural Committee in 1944 and the disappearance of the papers in 1950–52.

title: 1975 conveyance to BP Properties
text: Conveyance of 23 May 1975 from BP Pension Trust to BP Properties; HM Land Registry's file also lists a plan dated 23 February 1975.

title: Form 1C registration with statutory declaration
text: WA240304 registered on Form 1C, 'Not on a Recent Purchase — with Statutory Declaration in Support', edition 23 Feb 1983. HMLR: 'unaware of any dispute'.

title: Possession 'by the licence of BP Properties'
text: CA: 'from the time of her receipt of the letters, Mrs Buckler was in possession … by the licence of BP Properties Ltd', applying 'possession is never adverse if it can be referred to a lawful title'.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: 'Paper title' and 'registered proprietors'
text: CA: 'BP Properties Ltd, have the paper title to the farm, and indeed since November 1982 they have been the registered proprietors of it at HM Land Registry'.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: Exclusive possession, as his parents before him
text: CA: 'there is no doubt that Mr Buckler junior has exclusive possession of the farmhouse and garden, as his parents did before him, and no rent has been paid since 1953.'
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: The court's own doubt on unilateral licences
text: Dillon LJ: 'The claim that a unilateral licence can stop time running is a new one … it would enable a person … to keep his title alive for very many years until it suits him to evict.'
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: Assertion alone did not stop time
text: CA: WGR's advisers 'seem … to have supposed that, if they attended at the farmhouse from time to time and asserted Western Ground Rents' title, that was sufficient to prevent time running'; s.13 of the 1939 Act provides otherwise.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html

title: Graded 'marginally below the bar'
text: Cadw graded Great House 'marginally below the bar' for listing on 29 July 1988, four months before the eviction.

title: Demolition, 6 December 1988
text: 'The house and farm buildings were suddenly and completely demolished by B.P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy.'
source: HER GGAT02038s, as quoted by RCAHMW https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/rcahmw-correspondence/

title: A house that may have been medieval
text: HER: features 'suggested that the core of the house may have been medieval'; the survey stayed partial 'because of problems of access created by an ownership dispute'.
source: HER GGAT02038s, as quoted by RCAHMW https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/rcahmw-correspondence/

title: 'Fighting for 33 years'
text: South Wales Echo, 3 Dec 1988: the family had been fighting for 33 years to prove ownership of the farmhouse.

title: Mrs Nancy Buckler's sketch of old Llandough
text: Corbett of Cogan Pill papers hold 'Llandough [juxta-Penarth] sketch of former layout of part of village by Mrs. Nancy Buckler of great house farm, Llandough, with notes', c.1950.

title: Tree planting on Parcel A
text: Trees were planted on Parcel A as acts of ownership and occupation, from 1891 onwards (EV-0009; EV-0199 photograph of tree planting at the farm, date unknown).

title: H-A: war-ag use and no offer-back
text: War-ag direction in WW1 and WW2 touched the holding; land handed back went to the paper owner, never the Williams. Test: Glamorgan WAEC papers DSA/43/1 and DSA/43/3, farm survey MAF 32/73.

title: H-B: Parcel A taken in pieces
text: Water cut-off (c.1948–49), the 1949 re-grant, papers removed (1950–52), manor disposals (1950–57) and the 1955 execution read as one sequence. Test: the 1955 order plan and return.

title: H-C: one tenancy, as if 1928 never happened
text: Starting the record in 1916 with a 'whole farm' tenancy keeps the house inside a tenancy until 1955 and leaves 1877 and 1928 out. Test: the 1916 plan and the 1916–18 War Agricultural District Survey.

title: H-D: a Parcel B tenancy used to time Parcel A
text: The clock for the farmhouse was started at the end of Frederick's tenancy, which the 1939 plan shows as Parcel B. Test: the notice to quit and the plan filed with the 1955 possession application.

title: H-E: manor title versus parcel freeholds
text: Bute bought the manor in 1793 and is recorded as freeholder from the early 1800s, but no deed shows each of the 32–36 parcels reaching Bute. Test: NLW D219, D95/32–6, DB/E/1.

title: H-J: an estate built from assertions
text: BP's registered estate rests on recitals, a statutory declaration and a licence finding rather than a deed proving Parcel A passed to WGR. Test: the 1938 plan and WA240304 item 11.

title: 'Would have been destroyed'
text: Welsh Government ATISN 26-0010: 'No files were found and given the date range of your request, any routine records would have been destroyed in line with the corporate retention schedule applied at the time.'

title: Registry 'unaware of any dispute'
text: HM Land Registry, 25 May 2026: it 'did not receive or were aware of any interest … unaware of any dispute' at the 1982–83 first registrations, while BP's own 1974 action 'has never been finally heard'.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; reopen-loop ground R3 (work/reopen-loop/grounds.json) GHF-E153 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/ghf-e153-hmlr-stage-two-complaint-decision-25-may-2026/

title: The 1969 deed missing from both registry files
text: The 31 Dec 1969 WGR → BP Pension Trust conveyance, recited as BP's root, is not on either HM Land Registry first-registration file (WA231076, WA240304).
source: EV-0043 https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0043-wgr-bp-pension-trust-conveyance/; HM Land Registry letter 30 Jul 2026 https://wayback.bucklerfamily.estate/pdf/foi/2026-07-30_hmlr_first-registration-schedule.pdf ; reopen-loop grounds R1/R3/R4

title: The 1938 plan never produced
text: The 25 Dec 1938 conveyance and plan that would show whether Parcel A passed to WGR have not been produced by any party or archive found so far.

title: 'Agreed to buy' in Oct 1974, plan dated Feb 1975
text: CA treated BP Properties as able to license because the 31 Oct 1974 letters stated it 'had agreed to buy'; HM Land Registry's file lists a plan to the sale dated 23 February 1975.
source: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 (EV-0080) https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/1987/2.html; HM Land Registry letter 30 Jul 2026 https://wayback.bucklerfamily.estate/pdf/foi/2026-07-30_hmlr_first-registration-schedule.pdf ; reopen-loop grounds R1/R3/R4

title: Mary (Nancy) Williams dies at the farmhouse
text: Mary (Nancy) Williams, born at Great House Farm in 1913, died at the farmhouse on 26 March 1983, 31 days after the 23 February 1983 first-registration application for the farmhouse title. Her son William inherited and stayed in occupation.
